outcome: total fatty acid content in human milk
oleic acid (OA) content in human milk
palmitic acid (PA) content in human milk
linoleic acid (LA) content in human milk
saturated fatty acid (SFA) content in human milk
monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA) content in human milk
polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) content in human milk
a-linolenic acid (ALA) content in human milk
arachidonic acid (AA) content in human milk
docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) content in human milk
eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) content in human milk
cohort: The study included 41 lactating Filipino mothers from whom mid-morning human milk samples were collected.
finding: The total fatty acid content in human milk from Filipino mothers remained relatively constant over the first four months postpartum, with higher saturated fatty acids and lower essential fatty acids compared to other populations, and a decrease in human milk DHA levels when compared to previous reports from the Philippines.
